To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dystrophins-glycoprotein (DGC) complex binds to laminin in a Ca2+-dependent manner and is inhibited by heparan sulfate, and that dystroglycan, the laminin-binding protein of DGC, is present in nonmuscle cells and tissues.
dystrophin-gycoprotein complex binds laminin, and that dystroglycan of muscle and nonmuscle tissues binds laminin.
dystroglycan, the major component of the dystroglycan subcomplex of the dystrophins glycoprotein complex, binds to laminin in a Ca2+ dependent, NaCl-sensitive, heparin-inhibitable manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular structure and function of a complex of proteins associated with dystrophin, a protein that is mutated in the genetic disease Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
the role of the dystrophis-glycoprotein (DGC) complex in linking the extracellular matrix (ECM) with the cytoskeleton in striated muscle.

understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying the pathogenesis of muscular dystrophy and the role of dystroglycan and dystrophin in the maintenance of the structural and functional integrity of the muscle fiber.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the dystrophins, dystroglycans, sarcoglycans, and syntrophins together form a transmembrane complex that links the extracellular matrix to the actin cytoskeleton and that this complex is a target of mutations causing Duchenne muscular dystrophy.

the dystrophins and their associated glycoproteins are involved in a variety of cell-cell and cell-extracellular matrix interactions, including cell adhesion, signal transduction and cell motility, in a tissue-specific manner.
the dystrophins and dystroglycans are involved in the linkage of the actin based cytoskeleton to the extracellular matrix.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dystrophins are a family of cytoplasmic proteins that are associated with the actin cytoskeleton and are linked to the extracellular matrix via dystroglycan, a glycosylated transmembrane protein.
the dystrophins are a family of cytoskeletal proteins which are involved in the attachment of the extracellular matrices and the intracellular cytoskeletons of muscle and non-muscle cells.
dystrophin-gycoproprotein complex may play a role in linking the extracellular matrix to the actin cytoskeleton.
The main takeaway from our work is that
dystroglycan, a component of the dystroglycan complex, is a receptor for laminin.
dystroglycan, a component of the dystroglycan complex, can bind to laminin.
dystroglycan binds laminin and the dystrophin glycoprotein complex is linked to F-actin.
